title: Men in Black
year_note: The year is the original's. This recording is an AI-made soul cover posted on YouTube, and its upload title is all we know about it.

titles: Will Smith – Men In Black (1950's Soul Version)

notes.made: Poke and Tone of Trackmasters produced it, their first record with Smith, and it re-sings the chorus of Patrice Rushen's 1982 'Forget Me Nots' over that record's groove; Rushen, Terri McFaddin and bassist Freddie Washington share the writing credit. Coko of SWV sings the chorus and background vocals. It was Smith's first single without DJ Jazzy Jeff.
notes.context: Columbia put it out on June 3, 1997, as the lead single for Barry Sonnenfeld's film, which opened July 2 and grossed about $589 million worldwide. With no US retail single it was shut out of the Hot 100, yet it topped the airplay chart for four weeks and the UK singles chart for four. It later went on Smith's solo debut Big Willie Style, and won him the Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance over 'Hypnotize'.

listen_for.where: the bass line from the top
listen_for.note: Freddie Washington's bass from 'Forget Me Nots' is the hook the whole track rides on; a soul band only has to play it.
Coko sings a reworked Rushen chorus, so the sung melody in any cover is a 1982 R&B tune.

leads_to.title: Forget Me Nots
leads_to.why: The Elektra single under 'Men in Black', number four R&B and number eight in the UK, with Gerald Albright on tenor sax.
